title_lines: FIBER FUNCTORS OF EQUIVARIANTIZATIONS OF FINITE
metadata.abstract: LetGbe a finite group acting on a finite tensor categoryC. We classify fiber functors on the equivariantizationCG in terms of equivariant exact module categories overC, indexed by subgroups ofG. The data are a subgroupH⊆G and anH-equivariantC-module categoryMwhose underlyingC-module category is indecomposable, exact, and semisimple; they give a fiber functor precisely whenH acts transitively on the simple objects ofMand the stabilizer cocycle of one, hence every, simple object is non-degenerate. Through Tannaka–Krein reconstruction this describes realizations ofC G as the representation category of a finite-dimensional Hopf algebra, with no semisimplicity hypothesis onC. As applications, for odd primespwe determine the fiber functors onRep(Hp), whereHp denotes Nikshych’s semisimple Hopf algebra of dimension4p2 [Nik08]: there is one equivalence class if p≡3 (mod 4)and two ifp≡1 (mod 4). We also use the classification for gaugings to determine which non-pointed entries in the small-dimensional list of [GN25] are representation categories of semisimple factorizable Hopf algebras. 1.Introduction LetCbe a finite tensor category over an algebraically closed fieldkof characteristic zero. Afiber functoronCis ak-linear exact faithful tensor functorF:C→Vec k. Classical neutral Tannakian duality reconstructs affine group schemes from symmetric tensor categories equipped with a fiber functor [SR72, DM82]. In the non-symmetric setting relevant here, Tannaka–Krein reconstruction instead produces a Hopf alge- bra [JS91, Sch92, BV07]: for every fiber functorFon a finite tensor categoryC, there is a finite-dimensional Hopf algebraAF withC≃Rep(A F ), under whichFbecomes the forgetful functor [EGNO15, Theorem 5.3.12]. The fiber-functor problem is thus the problem ofHopf realization: deciding when a finite tensor category is the repre- sentation category of a finite-dimensional Hopf algebra, and counting the realizations arising from inequivalent forgetful functors.
